Three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some computers are phones.

All phones are calculators.

All calculators are i-pads.

**Conclusions:**

1. Some i-pads are computers.

2. All calculators are phones.

3. Some i-pads are phones.
questions.solution:

3. Some i-pads are phones → Follow → As All phones are calculators and All calculators are i-pads. So some i-pads are phones is definitely followed.

Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the state executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 153-167**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Articles of the Constitution of India that deal with the** State executive** are primarily **Articles 153 to 167.**
 
• These articles outline **the structure, powers, and functions of the state executive**, including the **Governor, Council of Ministers, Chief Minister, and other related provisions.**
 
• **Articles 153-167** of the Indian Constitution, which pertain to the state executive, are mentioned in **Part VI** - **The States of the Indian Constitution.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 153: **It states that there shall be a Governor for each state in India, appointed by the President of India.
 
• **Article 154: **This article establishes the office of the Governor as the constitutional head of the state executive.
 
• **Article 155: **Article 155 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment of the Governor of a state. .
 
• **Article 156: **Article 156 of the Constitution of India deals with the term of office of the Governor: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Article 157: **It describes the qualifications required for the appointment of the Governor.
 
• **Article 158: **The Governor shall not be a member of the Legislature or Parliament; shall not hold any office of profit, shall be entitled to emoluments and allowances. 
 
• **Article 159: **This article specifies the oath or affirmation to be taken by the Governor.** **
 
• **Article 160: **This article pertains to the discretionary powers of the Governor in matters related to the state executive.
 
• **Article 161: **It grants the Governor the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offence against state laws.
 
• **Article 162: **This article deals with the executive powers of the state and the extent of the executive power of the state government.
 
• **Article 163: **It empowers the Governor to exercise executive powers on behalf of the state government and defines the relationship between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.
 
• **Article 164: **This article deals with the appointment, term, and responsibilities of the Council of Ministers in the state.
 
• **Article 165: **It outlines the Advocate General for the state and their duties and qualifications.
 
• **Article 166: **This article deals with the conduct of government business and the duties of the Chief Minister and other ministers.
 
• **Article 167: **It specifies the duty of the Chief Minister to furnish information to the Governor regarding the administration of the state.

questions.question: In India, in which year was the National Food for Work Programme scheme launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2004.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Food for Work Programme (NFWP)** was launched in India in **2004.**
 
• It was a component of the **National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGA)** later renamed as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA).**
 
• The NFWP aimed to provide **food security** to rural populations by offering** employment opportunities in labour-intensive projects.**
 
• Workers participating in the NFWP** received food grains as remuneration **for their work.
 
• The NFWP was integrated into the broader framework of the **MGNREGA, expanding the scope and coverage of the employment guarantee program.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (**MGNREGA**).

 
 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA)** is a** social security and employment guarantee program** in India.
 
• It was enacted** in 2005** under the **National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA).**
 
• The program provides a **legal guarantee for 100 days of wage employment** in a financial year** to rural households.**
 
• MGNREGS focuses on **labour-intensive projects **such as** road construction, water conservation, and irrigation **to create employment opportunities and improve rural infrastructure.
 
• The scheme ensures timely payment of wages, provides social security provisions, and promotes transparency through mandatory public disclosure of information.

questions.question: Pick the odd one out (Hint: fiber crops).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rubber.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rubber is** not **a fiber crop.
 
• It is primarily **cultivated for latex production,** which is used in various industries, especially in the production of **rubber-based products.**
 
• In contrast, **cotton, hemp, and jute are fiber crops** that are specifically grown for their fibrous properties, which are used to make** textiles, ropes, and other related products.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kharif crops

 
 
• Kharif Crops are planted at the onset of the South-West monsoon, primarily in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, during the rainy season. 
 
• The sowing of these crops takes place between the months of June and July. 
 
• Upon reaching maturity, typically in October, these crops are harvested in the Autumn season. 
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include rice, cotton, corn, sugarcane, turmeric, pigeon pea, and more.
 
 
 
• Rabi crops
 
 
• Rabi Crops are cultivated during the winter season in regions with a subtropical climate.
 
• They include important crops like wheat, barley, oats, chickpeas, and peas.
 
• The Sowing of Rabi crops takes place between October and December.
 
• These crops require cooler temperatures and lesser rainfall compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Rabi crops play a crucial role in ensuring food security and contribute significantly to the agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• Zaid crops
 
 
• Zaid Crops are grown during the summer season in regions with a tropical climate.
 
• These crops are typically cultivated between the months of March and June.
 
• Zaid crops are known for their quick growth and shorter duration compared to Kharif and Rabi crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd, maize, and cowpea.
 
• These crops are often irrigated using modern techniques and are harvested before the onset of the monsoon season.

__
 
• **Saprotrophic nutrition** is the mode of nutrition in which **organisms obtain nutrients by decomposing dead and decaying organic matter.**
 
• Saprotrophs, also known as **decomposers**, secrete digestive enzymes to break down complex organic compounds into simpler substances.
 
• They absorb the nutrients from the decomposed matter, playing** a vital role in recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.**
 
• **Examples** of saprotrophs include** fungi **(such as mushrooms and moulds) and **certain bacteria.**

• **Autotrophic:**

 
 
• Autotrophic nutrition is the mode of nutrition in which organisms can** synthesize their own food using inorganic substances and an external energy source.**
 
• Autotrophs** convert sunlight or inorganic compounds into organic compounds** through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• They include **green plants, algae, and some bacteria.**
 
• Autotrophs are **primary producers in food chains**, serving as a source of energy for heterotrophs.
 
 
 
• **Heterotrophic:**
 
 
• Heterotrophic nutrition is the mode of nutrition in which **organisms obtain their food by consuming organic matter produced by other organisms.**
 
• Heterotrophs cannot **synthesize their own food and rely on consuming plants, animals, or other organic materials for nutrients.**
 
• Examples of heterotrophs include** animals, fungi** (except for a few species), and **most bacteria.**
 
• Heterotrophs play important roles **as consumers and decomposers** in food chains and nutrient cycles.
 
 
 
• **Monostrophic:**
 
 
• A monographic diet, also known as the** mono diet or single-food diet,** involves** eating only one food item or one type of food.**
 
• Examples of monotrophic diets include** consuming solely potatoes or apples or restricting oneself to fruits or meats.**
 
• Monotrophic diets may be followed for reasons such as **food faddism, crash dieting, initiating an elimination diet, or exploring extreme forms of alternative medicine.**

questions.question: Traditionally, the Budget documents classified total expenditure into ________.

• Budget documents classify total expenditures into **plan and non-plan expenditures.**
 
• **Plan expenditures** refer to the funds allocated for** specific programs, schemes, and projects** outlined in the budgetary plan.
 
• **Non-plan expenditures**, on the other hand, encompass general expenses such as **salaries, pensions, debt servicing, and maintenance costs.**
 
• This classification enables policymakers to **track and analyze spending patterns** to ensure efficient utilization of resources and effective implementation of developmental plans.

• Focused on achieving developmental goals in sectors like **education, health, infrastructure, etc.**
 
• Strategic allocation for long-term **objectives, economic growth, and poverty reduction.**
 
• Subject to evaluation and scrutiny to ensure effective utilization of funds.
 
 
 
• **Non-Plan Expenditure**:
 
 
• Covers** regular expenses **of the government*** *not** part of Five-Year Plans.
 
• Includes **administrative, operational, and maintenance costs.**
 
• Essential for** day-to-day functioning and provision** of services.
 
• Supports the overall governance and administration.

questions.question: Which of the following was the main demand of the peasant movement of Kheda?

options.text: Free irrigation facility to be provided

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **main demand of the peasant movement of Kheda** was **r****evenue collection be relaxed.**
 
• The Kheda Movement was a major civil disobedience movement in the **Kheda district of Gujarat**, India, led by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1918.**
 
• The movement was a **response to the oppressive taxation policies imposed by the British colonial government** on the peasants of Kheda, who were already suffering from** crop failures and economic hardships.**
 
• The peasants, led by Gandhi, decided to withhold the payment of taxes and launched a nonviolent protest against the government's unjust policies.
 
• The movement gained widespread support from various sections of society, and the unity and resilience displayed by the peasants **forced the British government to eventually negotiate and suspend the collection of taxes.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Champaran Satyagraha:**

 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha, which took place in **1917,** was another significant movement initiated by Mahatma Gandhi in the **Champaran district of Bihar, India.**
 
• The movement aimed to **address the exploitation of indigo farmers by British landlords** who forced them to grow indigo on a significant portion of their land, leaving them in abject poverty.
 
• Gandhi organized protests and supported the peasants in their struggle for fair treatment, improved living conditions, and the right to cultivate crops of their choice.
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha marked Gandhi's** first major nonviolent resistance movement in India **and played a crucial role in establishing his leadership and principles of Satyagraha.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement, launched by Mahatma Gandhi in **1920**, was a **nationwide campaign against British rule** in India.
 
• The movement aimed **to achieve swaraj (self-rule)** through nonviolent means and involved **boycotting British goods, institutions, and practices.**
 
• The movement received massive support from people across India, leading to the **withdrawal of cooperation from British institutions, including schools, courts, and the civil service.**
 
• However, the **movement was suspended in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident, **where violence erupted during a protest, leading Gandhi to call off the movement in order to maintain nonviolence as the guiding principle.
 
 
 
• **Dandi March or Salt Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the** Salt Satyagraha,** was a significant event in India's independence movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in **1930.**
 
• The march began with Gandhi and a group of followers embarking on a **240-mile journey** **from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, Gujarat, **to protest **against the British monopoly on salt production** and the imposed salt tax.
 
• The act of making salt from seawater at the coast of Dandi was a symbolic gesture challenging British laws, and it inspired people across India to participate in civil disobedience against the salt tax.
 
• The Dandi March** gained immense national and international attention,** further galvanizing the independence movement and highlighting the power of nonviolent resistance as a tool for change.

questions.question: In India, during October-November, with the apparent movement of the sun towards the south, the ______ over the northern plains becomes weaker.

__
 
• In India, during** October-November, **with the apparent movement of the sun towards the south, the **Monsoon trough** over the northern plains becomes weaker.
 
• The monsoon trough** is a low-pressure system that develops over the northern plains **of India during the **summer monsoon season**, which typically **lasts from June to September.**
 
• It is associated with the **seasonal shift **of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and the movement of the sun towards the south.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Upper-level trough** 

 
 
• An upper-level trough refers to a **region of relatively low atmospheric pressure** in the upper levels of the atmosphere.
 
• It is **not** specifically associated with the movement of the sun or the monsoon season in India.
 
 
 
• **Lee trough **-
 
 
• A lee trough is a **pressure trough that forms on the leeward side of a mountain range.**
 
• It is **not** directly related to the movement of the sun or the monsoon season in India.
 
 
 
• **Inverted trough **
 
 
• An inverted trough is a meteorological term that describes** a region of relatively low atmospheric pressure that extends vertically into the atmosphere.**
 
• It is **not** specifically associated with the movement of the sun or the monsoon season in India.

questions.question: A batsman makes a score of 97 runs in 15th inning and thus increases his average by 5. Find his average after 15th inning.

The batsman scores 97 runs in the 15th inning.

This increases his average by 5 runs.

**Formula used:**

Average = Total runs / Number of innings

**Solution:**

Let x be the batsman's average after 14 innings.

We know that the total runs scored by the batsman in 14 innings is 14x.

According to the question:

14x + 97 = 15(x + 5)

14x + 97 = 15x + 75

x = 22

Average after 15th innings = x + 22 = 5 + 22 = 27

questions.question: The population of a town increased from 145000 to 200000 in a decade. What will be the simple growth rate percent of population per annum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial population (P1) = 145,000

Final population after a decade (P2) = 200,000

Time (t) = 10 years

**We need to find:**

Simple growth rate per annum (r)

The formula for simple growth rate is given by:

r = ((P2 - P1)/P1)/t

Where:

P2 is the final population,

P1 is the initial population,

r is the simple growth rate,

t is the time (in years).

We plug in the values:

r = ((200000 - 145000)/145000) × 10

r = (55000 / 145000) × 10

r = 0.03793 × 10

r = 3.793%

**So, the simple growth rate of the population per annum is approximately 3.793%.**

questions.question: A can paint seven chairs in an hour and B can paint four chairs in an hour. Determine how much time they will require to paint 55 chairs when they work together.

A can paint 7 chairs in an hour.

B can paint 4 chairs in an hour.

**Formula:**

Total work = (A's rate)(B's rate)

Time = Total work/Combined rate

**Solution:**

The total work is 55 chairs. The combined rate is 7 + 4 = 11 chairs per hour. Therefore, the time required is:

Time = 55/11 = 5 hours

**Therefore, A and B will require 5 hours to paint 55 chairs when they work together.**

r is the interest rate

t is the time period

676/625 = (1 + 4/100)t

**Therefore, the time period is 2 years.**
